exposure: Type of antenatal care (midwife-led group vs. conventional individual)
cohort: Pregnant women in Queensland, Australia: 110 receiving midwife-led group antenatal care and 330 receiving conventional individual care
finding: Group antenatal care was not associated with a significant difference in mode of birth compared to conventional care.
mod_finding: Group care was associated with a lower risk of caesarean birth after controlling for previous births, with the highest chance for a vaginal birth being a woman who has had a previous vaginal birth and was in group care.
birth_weight: Measured, but specific values not reported
